conflicts.description: Repairing the fraying skybridges requires Windwright tether-silk and Tetherfolk binding-songs together, but the Conclave withholds silk over unpaid debts while the Tetherfolk refuse to sing for enclaves that let Mirabel fall. Each side blames the other as the spans go dark.
conflicts.name: The Silk-and-Song Standoff

conflicts.description: The Driftward Vow has begun severing mooring-lines in the Underspan, framing each frayed skybridge as a natural death. The Tetherfolk hunt them as saboteurs, but the Vow counts sympathizers in every enclave — including, perhaps, within the Chartwrights' own tower.
conflicts.name: The Quiet Cutting

conflicts.description: The Chartwrights' sealed surveys prove the drift can still be reversed — but only if every enclave cedes a measure of sovereignty to a renewed Concord. The Conclave suspects the Guild of manufacturing the crisis to crown itself keeper of the realm, and demands the Atlas be opened or the maps be taken.
conflicts.name: The Sealed Atlas

description: Aelora is a fractured realm of floating islands adrift on an endless sky, a fantasy world of wonder and slow-creeping peril. Long ago the land broke apart in the Sundering, and the scattered enclaves were bound together by the ancient skybridge network — living spans of solidified sky-light that hum when the wind moves through them. Now the skybridges are fraying, their songs thinning to whispers, and islands that once stood a morning's walk apart drift miles distant in a single season. The enclaves, long divided by old grievances and hoarded secrets, retreat behind their own horizons. Into this Waning comes a young cartographer whose charts reveal what no council will admit: the drift is accelerating, and if the skybridges fail entirely, Aelora will scatter into the Mists below forever. To mend the spans, the rival enclaves must be united — though some believe the drifting is destiny and will see the bridges break before they see them healed.

factions.description: The neutral order of mapmakers sworn to chart every drift, windway, and skybridge route in Aelora. Their maps are sacred ground no enclave may seize, but their habit of keeping the truest charts under seal has bred suspicion that they hoard the realm's survival for themselves.
factions.name: Guild of Chartwrights

factions.description: The weaver-lords of Vessandra who control the supply of lift-silk and tether-cord. Proud, mercantile, and bitter that the other enclaves take their craft for granted, they have begun withholding silk from skybridge repairs until old debts are honored.
factions.name: Windwright Conclave

factions.description: Hereditary keepers of the mooring-fields and hedge-shrines, the only people who still remember the full binding-songs that set a skybridge's roots. Diminished and overlooked, they know the spans are failing because fewer voices each year are left to sing them taut.
factions.name: The Tetherfolk

factions.description: A veiled fellowship of drifters, ex-sailors, and grieving families who believe the Sundering was a blessing and the skybridges a chain. They gather in the Underspan's ruins and quietly cut mooring-lines, convinced that letting the isles scatter is mercy, not ruin.
factions.name: The Driftward Vow

history.description: The unbroken land of Aelora tore apart in a single night of impossible storms, flinging its people onto islands cast across the open sky. Thousands were lost to the Mists, and the survivors lived isolated for a generation, each enclave believing itself the last.
history.name: The Sundering

history.description: The Chorus of Spanwrights — the ancestors of the Tetherfolk — discovered that song could pull sky-light into solid form, and sang the first skybridge into being between the two nearest isles. Word raced across the winds that no one need be alone again.
history.name: The First Skybridge

history.description: After decades of bridge-raids and map-wars, the three great enclaves met at Halcyon Spire and swore the Chartwrights' oath: maps neutral, skybridges shared, storm-tithes owed by all. The Concord that governed the archipelago was born.
history.name: The Treaty of Three Winds

history.description: When the skybridge to the orchard-isle of Mirabel snapped in a gale, no enclave would spare the silk or singers to raise another. Mirabel drifted beyond the charted winds and into the Mists within a year — the first isle lost since the Sundering, and the wound that seeded the Driftward Vow.
history.name: The Loss of Mirabel

history.description: In the present day, every skybridge in Aelora hums a half-tone flat and dims a shade each year. Charts drawn in spring are false by autumn. The Concord has not met in a decade, the tithes go unpaid, and a young cartographer's new survey proves the drift is accelerating toward a point of no return.
history.name: The Fading of the Spans

locations.description: The tallest island of the archipelago, crowned by a tower of white stone and sunglass where the Guild of Chartwrights keeps the Great Atlas. Every skybridge route is measured from its weathered observatory, and its hanging gardens of map-roses are said to bloom in the shapes of islands yet undiscovered.
locations.name: Halcyon Spire

locations.description: A sweeping terrace-island of windmills, kite-lofts, and lift-silk looms, home to the Windwright Conclave. Its people harvest the sky itself, weaving captured wind into the sailcloth and tether-silk that keeps commerce moving between the isles — a monopoly they guard jealously.
locations.name: Vessandra

locations.description: A green, brambled island of terrace farms and mooring-fields where the Tetherfolk anchor the skybridge roots deep into living soil. Its hedge-shrines mark every span ever raised, and its oldest families can still recite the binding-songs their ancestors sang to set the bridges fast.
locations.name: Thornfell

locations.description: The shadowed underside of the archipelago: a lattice of frayed skybridge roots, abandoned waystations, and drift-shrines clinging to the islands' keels. Those who believe the isles should be let go gather here in secret, and lost things — and lost people — tend to wash up in its hanging ruins.
locations.name: The Underspan

name: The Aelora Drift

rules.statement: A skybridge is not built but sung: it is a living lattice of solidified sky-light that holds only while voices keep its binding-song in tension. An unsung skybridge frays within a generation; a silenced one snaps within a season.

Every island drifts on the great wind-currents of Aelora. Two isles bound by a healthy skybridge hold their stations; without one, they can separate by miles in a single season, and no map stays true for long.
Nothing that falls below the Mists has ever returned. An island that loses its last skybridge and drifts beyond the charted winds is mourned as dead, and its name is struck from the Great Atlas.
All craft in Aelora runs on wind, sunglass lenses, lift-silk, and song. There are no explosive powders, no engines of combustion, and no flight save by kite, balloon, or tamed skysteed.
A sworn chart is neutral ground. By the Treaty of Three Winds, no enclave may seize, forge, or burn a Chartwright's map, and harming a mapmaker is the one crime every enclave still punishes alike.

Each enclave owes a storm-tithe of tether-silk and singing voices to the skybridge moorings every year. An enclave that withholds its tithe forfeits its vote in the Concord — and, some whisper, its right to stay tethered at all.
